title: Annotation-Efficient Individual Muscle Segmentation from Dixon MRI: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark of Pretraining and Fat-Fraction Guidance.
abstract: Measuring individual muscles and their fatty infiltration on Dixon MRI can support sarcopenia assessment, but manual annotation is time-consuming and annotated datasets are often small. This study investigated accurate individual-muscle segmentation with limited labelled data. Three datasets were used: an abdominal CT dataset of 300 subjects with adipose-tissue labels, a lower-limb Dixon MRI dataset of 25 subjects with 13 thigh and 9 calf muscles, and an independent cohort of 66 subjects for external testing. Network architecture, encoder pretraining, a Dixon-derived fat-fraction input, and a shared CT-MRI encoder were compared. A 2.5D model, subject-level cross-validation, zero-shot transfer, label-free domain adaptation, and few-shot adaptation were also evaluated. The best models reached Dice 0.947±0.017 for CT adipose tissue and 0.925±0.010 for thigh muscle; the best 2.5D model reached 0.928, while a reported 3D Attention-Res-V-Net reached 0.857 under a different protocol. Encoder pretraining helped most at the smallest budgets, with ImageNet performing best and comparably to CT-based pretraining at eight subjects. A shared CT-MRI encoder retained accuracy with 44% fewer parameters, and thigh-muscle volumes agreed closely with reference measurements (ICC (2,1)=0.998 ). On the external cohort, fine-tuning raised Dice from 0.11 zero-shot to 0.61, 0.76, and 0.88 with four, eight, and 46 labelled target subjects. The fat-fraction input improved segmentation only when very few subjects (two or four) were labelled. Encoder pretraining and efficient model sharing help when annotated MRI data are scarce. A small amount of target-domain annotation substantially improves cross-cohort transfer, and repeated subject-level validation is important for reliable evaluation.

title: Automated Multi-class Segmentation of Mandibular Odontogenic Cysts and the Mandibular Canal on CBCT Images Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework.
abstract: Mandibular odontogenic cysts can complicate surgical planning if located near the mandibular canal. Accurate delineation of both structures is therefore clinically important. This study presents a deep learning-based method for simultaneously segmenting mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. The developed method relies on a hybrid deep learning architecture integrating a ConvNeXt-Base encoder, a Dilated Context Block, a U-Net-based decoder, and a Deep Supervision mechanism. This framework simultaneously segments the mandibular canal and odontogenic cyst regions within the same architecture, promoting multi-scale contextual feature learning. We evaluated the performance of the proposed method using fivefold cross-validation experiments on a real-world clinical CBCT dataset comprising 103 patient images. We assessed segmentation performance using overlap-based metrics together with boundary-aware HD95 and ASSD metrics. The experimental results demonstrated that the model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 76.28% ± 1.83%. Excluding the background class yielded macro IoU and macro F1-score values of 64.46% ± 2.74% and 77.00% ± 1.89%, respectively. Meanwhile, the weighted IoU and weighted F1-score values were 78.71% ± 4.25% and 87.63% ± 2.63%, respectively. In boundary-based evaluations, the mandibular canal had an HD95 of 2.44 ± 2.98 mm and an ASSD of 0.45 ± 0.30 mm. The corresponding values for odontogenic cysts were 5.59 ± 3.65 mm and 1.43 ± 0.88 mm, respectively. These results suggest that the mandibular canal is more consistently delineated, while cyst segmentation remains more challenging, particularly at irregular and low-contrast boundaries. The proposed framework allows for the simultaneous and objective segmentation of mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal within a unified, multi-class CBCT analysis framework. By providing reproducible delineation of both structures, this method could serve as a technical foundation for future quantitative analyses of lesion-canal relationships. However, further validation using larger, multicenter, volumetric CBCT datasets is required before clinical translation.

title: Impact of Field Strength and Contrast Agents on Cardiac MRI Radiomic Features of the Myocardium and Blood Pool.
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of gadolinium-based contrast agents on cardiac MRI radiomic features across different magnetic field strengths. With Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval, eight healthy volunteers (38.5 ± 15.4 years; 4 males) underwent four consecutive cardiac MRI examinations using a Modified Look-Locker Inversion Recovery (MOLLI) sequence at 1.5T and 3T, with and without two contrast agents, gadopentetate dimeglumine (Gd-DTPA), and gadofosveset trisodium. Radiomic features were extracted from the myocardium and blood pool at the mid-ventricular level of the left ventricle using the first raw MOLLI image, corresponding to the shortest inversion time. Before contrast administration, switching from 1.5 to 3 T resulted in significant changes in 52% of myocardial and 56% of blood pool radiomic features. Contrast administration further altered radiomic feature values. At 1.5T, Gd-DTPA altered 42% of myocardial and 63% of blood pool features, whereas gadofosveset altered 73% and 85%, respectively. Similar patterns were observed at 3 T, with gadofosveset producing a greater proportion of altered features than Gd-DTPA (p < 0.05). Blood pool features were generally more sensitive to contrast administration than myocardial features. At 10 min after contrast administration, significant differences between the two contrast agents were observed in 48% of myocardial and 23% of blood pool features at 1.5T and in 72% and 60%, respectively, at 3 T. In conclusion, the administration and type of gadolinium-based contrast agents significantly alter cardiac MRI radiomic features across different magnetic field strengths. Future research should prioritize normalization strategies and evaluate feature robustness across larger patient populations to enhance the generalizability of cardiac radiomics.

title: SVF-net: A Dual-encoder Network with Adaptive Gated Fusion for Colorectal Polyp Segmentation.
abstract: Automatic colorectal polyp segmentation in retrospective still colonoscopy images remains challenging for small, low-contrast, partially occluded, or irregular lesions. We propose SVF-Net, a heterogeneous dual-encoder network combining a frozen SAM2 Hiera-L image trunk with a trainable MaxViT-RMLP-Small specialist branch. At four feature scales, the two streams are projected to a common width, spatially aligned, and reconciled by complementary channel-spatial gating before progressive decoding. Across five public benchmarks, three-run mean mDice is 0.922 on CVC-ClinicDB, 0.898 on Kvasir-SEG, 0.805 on CVC-ColonDB, 0.770 on ETIS-LaribPolypDB, and 0.896 on CVC-300. Matched projected-concatenation and fixed-weight ( G=0.5 ) controls retain the surrounding fusion path while removing input-dependent weighting; across ten matched training runs, adaptive gating gives higher mean mDice than both controls on all five datasets. Dataset-wide gate diagnostics on all 380 CVC-ColonDB and 196 ETIS cases indicate non-collapsed, scale- and region-dependent activations, while targeted one-factor sensitivity checks cover the MaxViT learning-rate multiplier, gate initialization, and auxiliary-loss weight. Matched per-case analyses further show that cross-domain gains are heterogeneous across lesion size, brightness, and an image-derived specular-reflection proxy. SVF-Net requires 92.8 ms per image (10.8 FPS) and 8.5 GB peak GPU memory on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 under the reported profiling protocol. The study evaluates retrospective static images only and does not establish real-time colonoscopy performance, prospective clinical effectiveness, or clinician benefit.

title: PW-GAN: Pseudo-Warping Field Guided GAN for Unsupervised Denoising of Fetal Brain MRI Images.
abstract: Fetal brain MRI commonly uses thick-slice acquisitions to mitigate motion artifacts and preserve in-plane image quality. Multiple motion-corrupted stacks of 2D slices can be retrospectively reconstructed into isotropic 3D volumes; however, volumes reconstructed from thicker slices generally exhibit lower image quality than those reconstructed from thinner slices because limited through-plane information results in residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. Existing post-reconstruction denoising methods are limited by their dependence on large-scale datasets comprising noisy-clean image pairs or insufficient modeling of inter-slice structural consistency. In this work, we propose a Pseudo-Warping Field Guided Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Network (PW-GAN), which formulates post-reconstruction denoising as unpaired translation between low- and high-quality MRI domains. By incorporating a pseudo-warping field module, our method significantly enhances inter-slice continuity in the reconstructed volumes while effectively suppressing residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. On simulated data, PW-GAN achieved a PSNR of 39.65 dB and an SSIM of 0.9932. On real clinical data, it reduced the inter-slice warping error by up to 40% compared with unsupervised baselines. These results demonstrate that PW-GAN outperforms existing unsupervised models and achieves performance comparable to several state-of-the-art supervised methods. Qualitatively, PW-GAN produced cleaner results with smoother inter-slice structural transitions while preserving anatomical structures, demonstrating its effectiveness in post-reconstruction denoising of fetal brain MRI acquired from thick-slice scans.

title: Interpretable fundus image-based glaucoma classification using aCDR-guided vascular tortuosity analysis.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interpretable hierarchical auxiliary classification framework for glaucoma-related fundus image analysis, with emphasis on transparent classification rationale for cases with intermediate aCDR values. Methods A MiT-B2-scSE U-Net was employed to jointly segment the optic disc and optic cup from fundus images, and the aCDR was calculated for initial image-level classification. Samples within predefined low- and high-aCDR ranges were directly classified, whereas samples in the intermediate-aCDR group underwent further analysis using peripapillary vessel segmentation and skeleton-based tortuosity quantification. To improve the reliability of vascular morphology assessment, a distance-aware topology-constrained loss function (DATCL) was introduced in the vessel segmentation stage to improve the segmentation accuracy of peripapillary vessels and improve the reliability of subsequent calculations. Results On the current REFUGE-based test set, the proposed MiT-B2-scSE U-Net achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (Dice) of 0.9254 and a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.8694 for joint optic cup-disc segmentation. For image-level glaucoma classification, the hierarchical aCDR-plus-vessel strategy achieved an accuracy of 91.25%, compared with 85.0% for the aCDR-only baseline and 66.25% for the vessel-only strategy. Conclusion The proposed framework suggests that combining optic cup-disc morphology with local vascular tortuosity may provide complementary information for interpretable glaucoma classification in fundus images with intermediate aCDR values. It provides a methodological avenue for deep learning-assisted glaucoma screening. Supplementary information The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13755-026-00484-5.

Purpose

This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interpretable hierarchical auxiliary classification framework for glaucoma-related fundus image analysis, with emphasis on transparent classification rationale for cases with intermediate aCDR values.

Methods

A MiT-B2-scSE U-Net was employed to jointly segment the optic disc and optic cup from fundus images, and the aCDR was calculated for initial image-level classification. Samples within predefined low- and high-aCDR ranges were directly classified, whereas samples in the intermediate-aCDR group underwent further analysis using peripapillary vessel segmentation and skeleton-based tortuosity quantification. To improve the reliability of vascular morphology assessment, a distance-aware topology-constrained loss function (DATCL) was introduced in the vessel segmentation stage to improve the segmentation accuracy of peripapillary vessels and improve the reliability of subsequent calculations.

Results

On the current REFUGE-based test set, the proposed MiT-B2-scSE U-Net achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (Dice) of 0.9254 and a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.8694 for joint optic cup-disc segmentation. For image-level glaucoma classification, the hierarchical aCDR-plus-vessel strategy achieved an accuracy of 91.25%, compared with 85.0% for the aCDR-only baseline and 66.25% for the vessel-only strategy.

Conclusion

The proposed framework suggests that combining optic cup-disc morphology with local vascular tortuosity may provide complementary information for interpretable glaucoma classification in fundus images with intermediate aCDR values. It provides a methodological avenue for deep learning-assisted glaucoma screening.

Supplementary information

The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13755-026-00484-5.

title: Super Resolution Reconstruction: A Strategy to Improve the Diagnostic Performance of Radiomics for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a key factor associated with high postoperative recurrence rate in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aims to evaluate the value of super-resolution (SR) reconstruction based on hepatobiliary phase (HBP) MR images for improving the accuracy of MVI prediction. Materials and methods A total of 544 patients with HCC from two medical centers between 2018 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed, including 450 patients in the training set, 51 in the internal validation set, and 43 in the external test set. Based on a lesion-aware 3D Restormer transformer architecture, SR reconstruction was performed using HBP MR images to generate super-resolution MR images. Tumor segmentations were automatically performed using the nnU-Net architecture and manually corrected by an experienced abdominal radiologist before radiomics feature extraction. Radiomics features were then extracted from original and SR images. Radiomics models based on original and SR images were developed to predict MVI status. Three machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and LightGBM, were used for model development. Results A total of 851 radiomics features were extracted from the original and SR images, respectively. Redundant features were filtered, and 50 radiomics features were selected using LASSO regression with cross-validated. For MVI prediction, the pooled areas under the receiver operating curves (AUCs) of radiomics model based on the original images were 0.710, 0.764, and 0.614 in the training, validation and test sets, respectively. The corresponding AUCs of the radiomics model based on the SR images were 0.855, 0.798, and 0.827, respectively. In the test set, the AUC of the radiomics model based on the SR images was higher than that based on the original images (0.827 vs. 0.614, p <0.001). Conclusion SR reconstruction can improve the diagnostic performance of radiomics models for predicting MVI in patients with HCC.
originalAbstract:
Rationale and objectives

Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a key factor associated with high postoperative recurrence rate in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aims to evaluate the value of super-resolution (SR) reconstruction based on hepatobiliary phase (HBP) MR images for improving the accuracy of MVI prediction.

Materials and methods

A total of 544 patients with HCC from two medical centers between 2018 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed, including 450 patients in the training set, 51 in the internal validation set, and 43 in the external test set. Based on a lesion-aware 3D Restormer transformer architecture, SR reconstruction was performed using HBP MR images to generate super-resolution MR images. Tumor segmentations were automatically performed using the nnU-Net architecture and manually corrected by an experienced abdominal radiologist before radiomics feature extraction. Radiomics features were then extracted from original and SR images. Radiomics models based on original and SR images were developed to predict MVI status. Three machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and LightGBM, were used for model development.

Results

A total of 851 radiomics features were extracted from the original and SR images, respectively. Redundant features were filtered, and 50 radiomics features were selected using LASSO regression with cross-validated. For MVI prediction, the pooled areas under the receiver operating curves (AUCs) of radiomics model based on the original images were 0.710, 0.764, and 0.614 in the training, validation and test sets, respectively. The corresponding AUCs of the radiomics model based on the SR images were 0.855, 0.798, and 0.827, respectively. In the test set, the AUC of the radiomics model based on the SR images was higher than that based on the original images (0.827 vs. 0.614, p <0.001).

Conclusion

SR reconstruction can improve the diagnostic performance of radiomics models for predicting MVI in patients with HCC.

title: VAE-based synthetic volume generation for trabecular bone microarchitecture.
abstract: Background and objective Micro computed tomography (microCT) enables detailed characterization of trabecular bone microarchitecture through quantitative morphological parameters. However, trabecular bone exhibits morphological variability across species, anatomical locations, bone types, and physiological or pathological conditions. Individual microCT datasets generally represent only a limited portion of this morphological variability, which may constrain the development and validation of quantitative descriptors, image-processing pipelines, and computational models. This study presents a Variational Autoencoder (VAE)-based framework for generating synthetic trabecular bone images, with the potential to support more comprehensive investigations of trabecular microarchitecture. Methods The VAE is trained on individual microCT slices and learns a three-dimensional latent space in which the ordered sequence of slices is mapped onto a continuous trajectory. Generating a synthetic volume reduces to i) defining a latent space trajectory and ii) decoding its points into 2D images ensuring inter-slice coherence without requiring any explicit 3D architecture. An interactive trajectory editor allows the user to manipulate, extend, or resample the latent path, providing full control over the morphology, length, and resolution of the synthetic volume. The reconstruction capability of the VAE was assessed by comparing the original microCT slices with their VAE-based reconstructions, and the original microCT-derived volume with the corresponding 3D volume obtained from the VAE-based reconstructed images, using 2D and 3D descriptors of trabecular microarchitecture. New sequences of synthetic images could be generated by modifying latent-space trajectories through the editor, thereby enabling the generation of multiple synthetic 3D volumes with controlled morphological variability. In this study, one such sequence was generated, and the corresponding 3D synthetic volume was characterized using microarchitectural parameters. The resulting values were then compared with those reported in the literature to assess the plausibility of the generated structure. Results Comparison of the morphological descriptors showed a high degree of similarity between the VAE-reconstructed and original microCT images. The corresponding 3D volumes also exhibited comparable morphological characteristics, indicating that the reconstruction process preserved the main structural features of the original microCT sample. Finally, the synthetic volume generated by synthetic VAE-based images exhibited microarchitectural parameter values comparable to those reported in the literature. Conclusion These results provide support for the ability of the proposed framework to generate synthetic trabecular microarchitectures with coherent structural features. Therefore, the framework can support data augmentation for deep-learning model training and more extensive investigations of trabecular microarchitecture. Future developments will focus on linking selected morphological descriptors to the three latent-space axes, thereby expanding the range of microarchitectural variability that can be generated and investigated.

title: The evolving role of cardiac CT: Emerging technologies and clinical impact.
abstract: Cardiac computed tomography (CT) has progressed from a non-invasive test primarily used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease into a comprehensive cardiovascular imaging platform for coronary artery disease, myocardial disease, valvular heart disease, and structural heart disease. Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is now endorsed as a first-line test in appropriately selected patients with stable chest pain or suspected chronic coronary syndromes because it can exclude obstructive disease, depict coronary atherosclerotic burden, support preventive treatment, and inform referral for invasive coronary angiography. At the same time, contemporary cardiac CT is moving beyond luminal stenosis. CT-derived fractional flow reserve and myocardial CT perfusion add a functional assessment of ischemia, whereas late iodine enhancement, CT-derived extracellular volume fraction, myocardial strain, and pericoronary fat attenuation index provide information on fibrosis, ventricular mechanics, vascular inflammation, and prognosis. Cardiac CT also has an established role in transcatheter valve therapy, left atrial appendage occlusion, and prosthetic valve assessment by providing a three-dimensional roadmap for device selection, access planning, and complication prediction. Photon-counting detector CT and artificial intelligence are further expanding the capabilities of cardiac CT through higher spatial resolution, spectral quantification, automated segmentation, quantitative plaque analysis, image reconstruction, and structured reporting. This review summarizes the evidence, technical foundations, clinical applications, and implementation challenges of contemporary cardiac CT, with an emphasis on its transition toward a decision-making platform for personalized cardiovascular care.

title: Temporal Changes in LGE-CMR Enhancement After Monopolar Biphasic Focal Pulsed Field Ablation for Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
abstract: Background Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel non-thermal ablation modality for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF). While chronic lesion formation after PFA has been described, data regarding acute lesion characteristics and lesion maturation remain limited. Objective To characterize acute and chronic lesion formation following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI using serial late-gadolinium-enhancement cardiovascular-magnetic-resonance-imaging (LGE-CMR). Methods Six consecutive patients with symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF underwent index PFA-guided PVI using the CENTAURI system and a focal point-by-point lesion delivery strategy. LGE-CMR was performed 1 day and 90±10 days after ablation. Quantitative assessment of regional and global left atrial (LA) enhancement was performed using a standardized segmentation protocol. Changes in enhancement burden and LA dimensions were analyzed between imaging timepoints. Results Among six patients at mean age 65±7 years, five patients (83%) had paroxysmal AF. Acute PVI was achieved in all patients without procedural complications. Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial temporal changes between acute and chronic imaging. Enhancement within the right pulmonary vein (PV) region decreased from 3.3±2.2% to 0.8±0.8%(p=0.030), while the proportion of enhanced tissue decreased from 24.1±13.5% to 5.7±5.8%(p=0.017). Similar reductions were observed around the left PVs (4.4±3.1%vs.1.4±1.2%, p=0.064). Posterior wall enhancement decreased from 2.4±1.1% to 0.3±0.3%(p=0.007) and global LA enhancement from 12.8±6.2% to 3.3±1.6%(p=0.013), while LA volume remained unchanged. Conclusion Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial enhancement reduction of acute lesions following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI, which remained largely confined to the PV antra and adjacent posterior wall, providing novel in-human insights into lesion maturation following focal PFA delivery.

title: Endoscopic transcanal repair of temporomandibular joint herniation into the external auditory canal: literature review.
abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) herniation into the external auditory canal is a rare condition associated with anterior canal wall defects, most commonly due to a patent foramen of Huschke, trauma, or infection. The clinical presentation is variable and often non-specific, which may lead to misdiagnosis. High-resolution computed tomography is crucial for accurate diagnosis and effective surgical planning. While open surgical repair remains standard, minimally invasive approaches have not been widely reported. An 81-year-old male presented with right-sided otalgia exacerbated by mandibular movement and unresponsive to topical and oral antibiotics. He was initially diagnosed with malignant otitis externa. Otoscopic and radiological evaluations revealed a soft-tissue mass protruding through an anterior external auditory canal defect, consistent with TMJ herniation. After acute inflammation resolved, the patient underwent endoscopic transcanal surgical repair under general anaesthesia. The herniated TMJ capsule was dissected, and the osseous defect was reconstructed using layered autologous conchal cartilage and perichondrium. The procedure was completed entirely through the endoscopic approach without external incisions. At the 6-month follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with complete graft integration and no recurrent herniation. Histopathological analysis excluded malignancy. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenge of TMJ herniation mimicking malignant otitis externa and demonstrates the feasibility of a fully endoscopic transcanal surgical approach for defect repair. The described minimally invasive technique offers a promising alternative to traditional open procedures, with reduced morbidity and favourable functional outcomes.

title: Artificial intelligence in diabetes: Clinical applications across the disease continuum.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping the landscape of diabetes mellitus (DM) care by enabling data-driven approaches to prediction, diagnosis, classification, and management. The growing availability of continuous biometric data from wearable technologies, combined with advances in machine learning, has created new opportunities to overcome limitations of traditional diabetes metrics and population-based care models. This review summarises current clinical applications of AI in DM, with a focus on translational relevance and, critically, on the level of validation and clinical readiness of each application. AI-based models have demonstrated improved performance in predicting DM onset and diabetes-related complications by integrating electronic health records, imaging data, and longitudinal clinical variables. In diagnosis and screening, AI offers non-invasive and scalable tools, including automated retinal screening systems and emerging digital biomarkers. Data-driven clustering approaches have further refined diabetes classification. In diabetes management, AI supports personalised glucose monitoring, insulin titration, pharmacological decision-making, and lifestyle interventions. Crucially, these applications differ markedly in maturity: autonomous retinal screening and closed-loop insulin delivery are approaching or have reached routine clinical use, whereas voice-based biomarkers and simulation-evaluated lifestyle systems remain proof-of-concept. Addressing challenges of generalisability, data quality, interpretability, and ethical governance through robust validation and explainable AI will be essential to realise the full potential of AI in precision, patient-centred diabetes care.

title: Nucleic acid technologies in crustacean disease management: Diagnostics, therapeutics, and surveillance.
abstract: Crustacean aquaculture, particularly shrimp, crab, and lobster production, contributes around US$10 billion annually to the global food supply but remains highly vulnerable to viral and bacterial diseases. Pathogens such as White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV), Yellow Head Virus (YHV), Taura Syndrome Virus (TSV), and Vibrio species continue to cause substantial economic losses, and conventional management based on visual inspection, histopathology, and antimicrobial treatment is often slow and insensitive. This review examines how nucleic acid technologies are reshaping diagnostics, therapeutics, and surveillance in crustacean health management. Molecular diagnostic platforms including PCR, quantitative PCR, reverse transcription PCR, loop mediated isothermal amplification, recombinase polymerase amplification, and multiplex assays allow rapid, sensitive, and specific detection of pathogens, often before clinical signs appear. RNA interference shows strong therapeutic promise against viral pathogens, with experimental studies reporting 40 to 80% reductions in cumulative mortality, although stability, dosing, delivery, and production cost continue to limit commercial use. CRISPR (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats) and Cas (CRISPR-associated) has emerged as a powerful platform for functional genomics, immune gene characterisation, and the future development of disease resistant strains, though application in crustaceans remains largely proof of concept. Environmental DNA and molecular biosurveillance enable early pathogen detection through water and sediment sampling, supporting proactive biosecurity and precision aquaculture. Persistent barriers include scalability, infrastructure gaps in producing regions, regulatory uncertainty, and public acceptance. Future progress will rely on improved delivery systems, expanded crustacean genomic resources, and integration of molecular tools with digital farm management to deliver sustainable disease control.

title: A diagnostic model integrating clinical, magnetic resonance imaging, and arthroscopic findings accurately identified hypermobile lateral meniscus: Development and internal validation.
abstract: Background To develop and internally validate a diagnostic model for hypermobile lateral meniscus (HLM) integrating clinical symptoms, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings, and dynamic arthroscopic assessment. Methods A retrospective diagnostic model study was performed, including 100 consecutive patients evaluated for suspected lateral meniscal pathology at a tertiary knee surgery center. All patients underwent standardized clinical examination, preoperative MRI, and arthroscopic assessment of lateral meniscal mobility, which served as the reference standard. Candidate predictors were restricted to preoperative clinical and MRI variables, including intermittent locking, posterolateral McMurray test, meniscocapsular gap, and suspected meniscotibial discontinuity. Arthroscopic findings were used exclusively to establish the reference-standard diagnosis and were not entered into the diagnostic model. A penalized logistic regression model with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) selection was used to identify independent predictors and construct the Hypermobile Meniscus Index (HMI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, and robustness was assessed with Monte Carlo simulation. Results HLM was confirmed arthroscopically in 47% of patients. The final model included five independent predictors and demonstrated excellent discriminative performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.84 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.83-0.95). At the optimal cut-off (≥5 points), sensitivity was 81%, specificity 79.2%, positive predictive value 77.6%, and negative predictive value 82.4%. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities (calibration slope 0.94, intercept 0.03; and Brier score 0.13). Bootstrap validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.82. Monte Carlo simulation confirmed stability of model performance across varying prevalence scenarios, with consistent sensitivity and specificity ranges. Conclusion A diagnostic model combining clinical and MRI findings demonstrated internally validated performance for identifying HLM as defined by dynamic arthroscopy. The HMI provides a structured framework to improve preoperative recognition and guide targeted arthroscopic assessment in patients with mechanical lateral compartment symptoms and inconclusive imaging. External validation is required prior to routine clinical implementation. Level of evidence Level III, diagnostic study.

title: Large-domain histology-based diffusion MRI simulation via independent local simulations.
abstract: Diffusion MRI simulations based on realistic tissue microstructure provide a means to validate biophysical models and optimize acquisition protocols, but their computational cost restricts most studies to domains far smaller than a clinical voxel. The objective of this study was to develop an automated and scalable framework that converts whole-slide histology into diffusion MRI simulations at clinically relevant spatial scales while remaining feasible on standard workstation hardware. We present an end-to-end pipeline integrating two-dimensional whole-slide cell segmentation, mesh generation, and finite element Bloch-Torrey simulation. To enable simulations at large spatial scales without prohibitive memory growth, we introduce a subdomain tiling strategy in which the tissue domain is partitioned into extended subdomains simulated independently under no-flux boundary conditions. Signals are aggregated only from the central regions of each subdomain to minimize boundary artifacts. For an 800 μm × 800 μm histology-based domain, the aggregated signal differed by 0.07% from the corresponding full-domain finite element simulation while reducing wall-clock time from several days to hours and maintaining bounded memory usage independent of global domain size. When applied to a 2016 μm × 2016 μm heterogeneous region approximating the in-plane dimensions of a clinical voxel, the apparent diffusion coefficient obtained from the full domain differed from values computed in smaller dense and sparse subregions, demonstrating the influence of structural heterogeneity at clinically relevant scales on derived diffusion metrics. The proposed framework establishes an automated and memory-stable approach for generating diffusion MRI simulations directly from routine histology.

title: Visualization of post-STEMI myocardial infarction and microvascular obstruction with non-contrast, free-breathing whole- heart iT<sub>2</sub>prep-IR BOOST.
abstract: Background Clinical adoption of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for risk stratification in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is often limited by long scan times and the requirement for breath-holding and contrast agents. Objectives This study aimed to validate a non-contrast, free-breathing 3D whole-heart T1/T2 CMR method (iT 2 prep-IR BOOST) for rapid assessment of myocardial injury in STEMI patients, hypothesizing that this technique provides promising diagnostic accuracy and quantitative assessment to conventional contrast-enhanced CMR. Methods A free-breathing 3D isotropic whole-heart iT 2 prep-IR BOOST sequence was performed with a scan time of <8minutes. Sixty-four STEMI patients underwent CMR, including iT 2 prep-IR BOOST, clinical T2-STIR, late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and T1/T2 mapping. The diagnostic performance of iT 2 prep-IR BOOST was evaluated against LGE and T2-STIR to assess myocardial infarction (MI), microvascular obstruction (MVO), and edema. Subgroup analyses further investigated the association between MVO detected by iT 2 prep-IR BOOST and left ventricular (LV) remodeling at 1-year follow-up. Results In 60 STEMI patients, the acquisition was completed in 7.2 ± 0.6min as a single free-breathing 3D whole-heart scan. Patient-level analysis showed high sensitivity and specificity for MVO (100.0% / 87.5%) and segmental MVO detection (95.8% / 97.8%). T 2 prep-IR BOOST yielded robust image contrast for MI comparable to LGE, while offering comparable edema visualization to T2-STIR. Volumetric and transmurality quantifications of MVO, MI, and edema showed excellent agreement with reference standards (all r > 0.90, p < 0.001), supported by significant biophysical correlations with native T1/T2 values (p < 0.001). Furthermore, in a 1-year follow-up cohort (n=51), baseline T 2 prep-IR BOOST-derived MVO volume was associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling, showing significant correlations with both ΔLVEDVI (r = 0.305, p = 0.029) and ΔLVESVI (r = 0.293, p = 0.037). Conclusions In this preliminary single-center study, iT 2 prep-IR BOOST showed promising diagnostic performance and close quantitative agreement with conventional LGE and T2-STIR in stable STEMI patients. Further prospective validation in larger, independent, and more heterogeneous cohorts, including patients unable to undergo contrast-enhanced CMR, is required before this technique can be considered an alternative to standard LGE and T2-weighted sequences.

title: Understanding Colorectal Cancer Screening Gaps Among Adults Aged 45-49.
abstract: Introduction The United States Preventative Task Force recommends initiating colorectal cancer (CRC) screening at age 45, but screening rates among 45-49 y-olds has been lower than older age groups. Reasons for low screening rates among younger individuals are not clear. Methods Using Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 2022 to 2024, we investigated factors associated with CRC screening among adults aged 45-49; stratified analyses were conducted among the insured and uninsured. Among screened individuals, associations with undergoing endoscopy versus another screening modality were studied. We characterized preventative care behaviors including seeking primary care, time since last checkup, and completion of other age-appropriate cancer screening. Results Of 50,132 individuals, 21,566 (42.6%) underwent CRC screening. Those with primary care physicians had higher odds of screening (odds ratio = 1.71; 95% confidence interval = 1.47-1.98, ref: no primary care physician), but increasing time since one's last visit was associated with decreasing odds of screening at all time intervals (5+ y ago: odds ratio = 0.29; 95% confidence interval = 0.23-0.38, ref: <1 y). Lower income, rural residence, no insurance, and lower educational attainment were associated with lower odds of screening. CRC screening was completed in only 41.3% of women who had mammograms and 48% who were screened for cervical cancer. Conclusions Uptake of CRC screening lags in adults aged 45-49, with differences in socioeconomic factors and preventative care utilization. A majority of eligible but unscreened individuals accessed other age-appropriate cancer screening tests, directing focus to patient- and provider-specific factors as potential targets for intervention.

title: Postembolization CT Digital Subtraction Angiography for Assessing Spinal Tumor Devascularization: Concordance With Catheter Angiography and Association With Surgical Blood Loss.
abstract: Background context The adequacy of preoperative embolization for spinal tumors is commonly assessed using selective catheter angiography, but standardized criteria remain lacking. Postembolization CT digital subtraction angiography (CT-DSA) may provide complementary whole-tumor assessment of residual enhancement. Purpose To evaluate concordance between postembolization CT-DSA and catheter angiography, examine associations between CT-DSA findings and surgical blood loss, and identify factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA findings. Design Retrospective single-center observational cohort study. Patient sample Seventy-two adults who underwent preoperative embolization and postembolization CT-DSA before spinal tumor surgery, including 62 patients with metastatic tumors and 10 with primary spinal neoplasms. Outcome measures Concordance between CT-DSA and catheter angiographic devascularization categories, estimated blood loss (EBL), quantitative CT-DSA peak enhancement index, and factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories. Methods Postembolization devascularization was classified as complete, subtotal, or partial using modality-specific criteria. Concordance was evaluated using cross-classification and linearly weighted κ. Associations between CT-DSA findings and EBL were analyzed in patients with metastatic tumors using multivariable regression adjusted for surgical invasiveness and baseline angiographic hypervascularity. Proportional-odds ordinal regression was used to explore factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories. Results CT-DSA and catheter angiography assigned the same devascularization category in 39 of 72 patients (54.2%), with moderate weighted concordance (κ=0.423; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.265-0.580). Among patients with metastatic tumors, median EBL was 1,000 mL for complete, 1,650 mL for subtotal, and 1,975 mL for partial devascularization (P=.214). The adjusted overall association between CT-DSA category and EBL was not statistically significant (P=.167). Compared with complete devascularization, partial devascularization showed a directionally higher but imprecise EBL estimate (adjusted EBL ratio, 1.582; 95% CI, 0.861-2.907; P=.139). The quantitative peak enhancement index was not associated with EBL. Greater baseline angiographic hypervascularity (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per grade, 3.243; 95% CI, 1.782-5.902) and a same-level spinal artery (adjusted OR, 10.236; 95% CI, 2.477-42.293) were associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories. Conclusions Postembolization CT-DSA showed moderate concordance with catheter angiography and may complement selective angiographic assessment by depicting residual enhancement throughout the tumor. originalAbstract:
Background context

The adequacy of preoperative embolization for spinal tumors is commonly assessed using selective catheter angiography, but standardized criteria remain lacking. Postembolization CT digital subtraction angiography (CT-DSA) may provide complementary whole-tumor assessment of residual enhancement.

Purpose

To evaluate concordance between postembolization CT-DSA and catheter angiography, examine associations between CT-DSA findings and surgical blood loss, and identify factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA findings.

Design

Retrospective single-center observational cohort study.

Patient sample

Seventy-two adults who underwent preoperative embolization and postembolization CT-DSA before spinal tumor surgery, including 62 patients with metastatic tumors and 10 with primary spinal neoplasms.

Outcome measures

Concordance between CT-DSA and catheter angiographic devascularization categories, estimated blood loss (EBL), quantitative CT-DSA peak enhancement index, and factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories.

Methods

Postembolization devascularization was classified as complete, subtotal, or partial using modality-specific criteria. Concordance was evaluated using cross-classification and linearly weighted κ. Associations between CT-DSA findings and EBL were analyzed in patients with metastatic tumors using multivariable regression adjusted for surgical invasiveness and baseline angiographic hypervascularity. Proportional-odds ordinal regression was used to explore factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories.

Results

CT-DSA and catheter angiography assigned the same devascularization category in 39 of 72 patients (54.2%), with moderate weighted concordance (κ=0.423; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.265-0.580). Among patients with metastatic tumors, median EBL was 1,000 mL for complete, 1,650 mL for subtotal, and 1,975 mL for partial devascularization (P=.214). The adjusted overall association between CT-DSA category and EBL was not statistically significant (P=.167). Compared with complete devascularization, partial devascularization showed a directionally higher but imprecise EBL estimate (adjusted EBL ratio, 1.582; 95% CI, 0.861-2.907; P=.139). The quantitative peak enhancement index was not associated with EBL. Greater baseline angiographic hypervascularity (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per grade, 3.243; 95% CI, 1.782-5.902) and a same-level spinal artery (adjusted OR, 10.236; 95% CI, 2.477-42.293) were associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories.

Conclusions

Postembolization CT-DSA showed moderate concordance with catheter angiography and may complement selective angiographic assessment by depicting residual enhancement throughout the tumor. Partial devascularization showed a directionally higher but imprecise association with surgical blood loss in metastatic tumors and requires further validation.

title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Combined With Regional Division for Differentiating Benign and Metastatic Lymph Nodes.
abstract: Objective Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables high-resolution visualization of lymph node microvasculature. However, most previous studies rely on whole-node analysis, which may overlook spatial heterogeneity and be affected by confounding factors. This prospective single-center study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of ULM combined with regional analysis for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes. Methods A total of 104 lymph nodes from patients with sonographically suspicious lymph nodes were included. All lymph nodes underwent ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy, which served as the reference standard for classification (benign or metastatic). Each lymph node was divided into central, peripheral, and global regions, and ULM quantitative parameters were extracted. Regional ratio features were calculated. Feature selection was performed using univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and backward stepwise logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold stratified cross-validation, 2000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis (DCA), and clinical impact curve (CIC). Results Three diagnostic models were constructed: a conventional ultrasound (US) model, a ULM model, and a combined US-ULM model. The combined model demonstrated the best discriminative performance with an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI: 0.7875-0.9320), followed by the ULM model (AUC = 0.833, 95% CI: 0.7464-0.9108) and the US model (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.6219-0.8285). In multivariable analysis, SD.Density_C_P (OR =0.0578, p = 0.012), FD_C_P (OR = 0.8847 per 0.01 increase, p = 0.003), and peripheral vascular pattern (OR = 10.9501, p < 0.001) were identified as significant predictors of lymph node metastasis. At optimal cut-off values, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 0.733 and specificity of 0.915. Conclusion The proposed region-based ULM model combined with conventional ultrasound provides an improved quantitative approach for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes in patients with sonographically suspicious lymphadenopathy.

title: Image-guided focused ultrasound for non-invasive modulation of superficial and deep tissues.
abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) enables non-invasive, spatially precise modulation of biological tissues. This protocol describes assembly, calibration, and implementation of a diagnostic ultrasound-guided FUS (dUS-FUS) platform for real-time targeting of superficial and deep tissues in small-animal models. We demonstrate reversible sciatic nerve modulation in a rat acute pain model and assess sensory and motor functions using behavioral tests. The platform provides a reproducible workflow for image-guided tissue modulation and can be adapted to diverse preclinical applications. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Sangwan et al. 1 , 2 .

title: Structural network alterations and peripheral immune-inflammatory dysregulation define distinct subtypes of major depressive disorder with prognostic implications.
abstract: Background Immune-inflammatory dysregulation and cortical structural vulnerability have been increasingly implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, how they interact with each other, and whether immune heterogeneity in MDD is systematically organized by structural networks, remain unclear. Methods Genome-wide association studies data of MDD, gray matter volume (GMV) phenotypes, and 19 immune-related traits were utilized to assess causal relationships. A prospective cohort comprising 122 patients with MDD and 66 healthy controls underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging and assessment of 40 inflammatory and immune-related markers. Individualized structural covariance network analysis, machine-learning approaches, and survival analyses were used to identify neurobiological subtypes and evaluate treatment outcomes. Results Genetically predicted MDD was associated with lower levels of circulating IGF-1 ( p FDR = 0.013). Levels of IL-5 and leptin were negatively associated with GMV alterations in the right cingulate gyrus and bilateral putamen, respectively ( p FDR < 0.05). Structural covariance abnormalities were predominantly localized to connectivity between the default mode and limbic networks and within the limbic network in MDD, and they were classified into a hypoconnectivity subtype ( n = 49) and a hyperconnectivity subtype ( n = 73). The hypoconnectivity subtype exhibited greater anxiety and anhedonia symptoms, whereas the hyperconnectivity subtype showed broadly elevated inflammatory and immune state and achieved antidepressant response more rapidly during follow-up ( p = 0.032). Conclusions This study supports a bidirectional immune-brain framework in MDD and suggests that structure-derived subtypes classify different immune signaling heterogeneity, which may provide a biologically informed basis for stratification and prognosis in MDD.

title: Applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants: implications for respiratory distress syndrome and bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a promising bedside imaging modality in neonatal intensive care units, offering real-time assessment of lung aeration without exposure to ionizing radiation. These advantages are particularly relevant for preterm infants, who are vulnerable to cumulative radiation exposure and evolving pulmonary disease. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the functional clinical applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants. We focus on how LUS has been studied to guide early respiratory management, predict the need for surfactant and escalation of respiratory support, assess extubation readiness, identify infants at increased risk for bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and monitor disease trajectory and response to therapy throughout the NICU course, including emerging data on longer-term respiratory outcomes. While available studies demonstrate promising diagnostic and prognostic value, interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, scoring systems, timing of assessment, and operator dependence. Further multicenter studies with standardized protocols are needed to define the role of LUS in routine neonatal respiratory care.

title: Shared cortical morphometry and molecular signatures across depression and physical diseases.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly comorbid with physical diseases, suggesting shared neurobiological mechanisms. However, the common structural and molecular substrates underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood. We analyzed multimodal MRI data from 577 patients (MDD, asthma, fibromyalgia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, type 2 diabetes) and 275 healthy controls, constructed individual morphometric similarity networks (MSN) to identify shared cortical alterations, and applied principal component analysis with multiscale molecular annotation (transcriptomic, cell-type, neurotransmitter, and cognitive mapping) to characterize underlying mechanisms. All patient groups exhibited regional MSN abnormalities. A shared MSN pattern emerged, featuring increased similarity in visual and somatomotor regions and decreased similarity in ventral attention, limbic, and default mode networks, and was replicated in independent cohorts. This pattern was significantly associated with spatial gene expression enriched for synaptic signaling, membrane potential regulation, and neuronal architecture, with predominant expression in excitatory/inhibitory neurons and astrocytes. It further mapped onto specific neurotransmitter systems, with exploratory cognitive decoding suggesting possible relevance to emotion and social cognition. Related genes overlapped with known risk loci for Alzheimer's disease and bipolar disorder. These findings identify a robust across diseases cortical MSN phenotype linked to convergent molecular and neurochemical correlates, offering a framework for studying shared vulnerability and transdiagnostic mechanisms across depression and physical diseases.

title: Rare prostate cancer histologies: detection, characteristics and treatment.
abstract: Relatively rare histologies of prostate cancer collectively account for <5% of all prostate cancers and comprise mucinous adenocarcinoma, intraductal carcinoma, ductal adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine prostate cancer (including treatment-emergent small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma), sarcomatoid carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma. These histologies have distinct morphological, molecular and clinical features from each other and the most common histological type, acinar adenocarcinoma. The perceived rarity of these histologies often reflects sampling limitations rather than biological prevalence, as many treatment-emergent phenotypes are seldom encountered in routine practice owing to the infrequent use of metastatic biopsies. These histologies demonstrate aggressive behaviour, atypical metastatic patterns and reduced responsiveness to conventional therapies. Despite their clinical importance, these entities remain under-represented in standard guidelines and clinical trials. Histological types and subtypes, such as ductal, mucinous, intraductal, neuroendocrine and sarcomatoid carcinomas, pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, and conventional screening with PSA exhibits limitations, so they are often diagnosed at advanced stages. Multiparametric MRI, immunohistochemistry and genomic profiling are crucial tools for accurate recognition and risk stratification. Histological type-specific genomic alterations, including DNA repair deficiencies, RB1 and TP53 loss, and mismatch repair mutations, provide potential therapeutic opportunities, but treatment recommendations are still largely extrapolated from acinar adenocarcinoma. Limited retrospective data suggest worse outcomes for patients with a rare histology than those with typical acinar adenocarcinoma, highlighting the urgent need for prospective registries and dedicated clinical trials. Rare histologies of prostate cancer are an under-recognized source of morbidity and mortality. Improved diagnostic precision, incorporation of molecular profiling and collaborative data collection efforts are essential to develop evidence-based strategies.

These histologies demonstrate aggressive behaviour, atypical metastatic patterns and reduced responsiveness to conventional therapies. Despite their clinical importance, these entities remain under-represented in standard guidelines and clinical trials. Histological types and subtypes, such as ductal, mucinous, intraductal, neuroendocrine and sarcomatoid carcinomas, pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, and conventional screening with PSA exhibits limitations, so they are often diagnosed at advanced stages. Multiparametric MRI, immunohistochemistry and genomic profiling are crucial tools for accurate recognition and risk stratification. Histological type-specific genomic alterations, including DNA repair deficiencies, RB1 and TP53 loss, and mismatch repair mutations, provide potential therapeutic opportunities, but treatment recommendations are still largely extrapolated from acinar adenocarcinoma. Limited retrospective data suggest worse outcomes for patients with a rare histology than those with typical acinar adenocarcinoma, highlighting the urgent need for prospective registries and dedicated clinical trials. Rare histologies of prostate cancer are an under-recognized source of morbidity and mortality. Improved diagnostic precision, incorporation of molecular profiling and collaborative data collection efforts are essential to develop evidence-based strategies.

title: Perivascular spaces are associated with T cell trafficking and may have prognostic relevance in brain metastases.
abstract: Background Perivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear. Methods In this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale. Tumor immune infiltration, vascular features, and immune cell phenotypes were assessed by immunohistochemistry and spectral flow cytometry and correlated with clinical outcome. Results Here we show that high PVS burden in the centrum semiovale region, but not in the basal ganglia, were significantly associated with improved overall survival. High PVS are linked to increased presence of tumor-infiltrating cytotoxic T cells-most of which exhibited an activated/exhausted phenotype, indicated by PD-1- and Fas-positivity-was likewise prognostically favorable. Moreover, these cells showed elevated expression of the migration marker CXCR3, as well as Granzyme B/IFNγ consistent with effector polarization. High PVS were additionally associated with a higher M1/M2-like macrophage ratio, which showed similar prognostic relevance as high vascular density, suggesting enhanced blood supply and immune cell recruitment. Conclusion These findings could establish PVS as a non-invasive imaging marker of anti-tumor immunity and prognosis in patients with brain metastasis, underscoring their potential as biomarkers for immune activity and therapeutic monitoring.

title: Giant Multiloculated Cystic Trochlear Nerve Schwannoma Between the Tentorial Leaflets: Case Report and Systematic Review.
abstract: Background Trochlear nerve schwannomas (TNSs) are exceptionally rare benign tumors, accounting for a very small fraction of intracranial schwannomas. Due to their deep locations and slow growth, they often reach a considerable size before diagnosis. Giant or multiloculated cystic variants are exceptionally uncommon and present significant diagnostic and surgical challenges. Methods A 32-year-old female presented with headache and dizziness but no diplopia. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a giant multiloculated cystic lesion extending from the posterior fossa to the right temporal lobe, causing obstructive hydrocephalus. The mass was removed through a right paramedian supracerebellar transtentorial approach under intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. The tumor was confined between the two tentorium leaflets with the trochlear nerve entering and exiting the lesion. Gross total resection was achieved with an uneventful postoperative course. Histopathology confirmed a World Health Organization Grade I schwannoma with Antoni A-B architecture and diffuse S-100 positivity. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines, identifying forty-six surgically treated cases, analyzed together with the present case (n = 46). Results Mean age was 44.7 years with an approximately equal sex distribution. Most tumors (76.1%) were located in the ambient or crural cisterns, followed by the quadrigeminal cistern (10.8%) and cisterno-cavernous region (8.7%). Diplopia and trochlear nerve palsy were the most common presenting symptoms. Gross total resection was achieved in 80.4% of patients, while postoperative trochlear palsy occurred in 60.8%. No malignant transformation or early recurrence was reported. Conclusion This case represents one of the largest TNSs described and the second known lesion arising between the tentorial leaflets. Awareness of this unique anatomic configuration is essential for accurate preoperative diagnosis and surgical planning. A meticulous, anatomy-guided microsurgical approach enables complete resection while preserving neurological function in select cases.

title: Benchmarking 3D U-Net variants for volumetric segmentation of the substantia nigra and brain ageing related analysis using 7T MRI.
abstract: Objective: Accurate segmentation of the substantia nigra (SN) is essential for assessing its structural integrity and volumetric changes in Parkinson's disease and brain aging. However, it remains challenging due to SN's small size, deep location, and low contrast on conventional MRI. This study benchmarked six U-Net variants baseline 3D U-Net, ResU-Net, SE-U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and U-Net 3+ for SN segmentation using ultra-high-field 7 T MRI. Methods T1-weighted MP2RAGE images from the ATAG dataset (53 healthy subjects: 31 train, 7 validation and 15 test). Six architectures were evaluated: 3D U-Net, ResU-Net, SE-U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and U-Net 3+.Performance was evalauted with Dice score, IoU, 95% HD95, ASSD, and also age-stratified analysis was considered for analysing the robustness of model across young, middle-aged, and elderly cohorts. Results While ResU-Net achieved the highest overlap metrics (Dice = 0.763, IoU = 0.618), where the baseline 3D U-Net outperformed all variants in boundary accuracy (HD95 = 13.85 mm, ASSD = 20.15 mm). The U-Net 3+ and SE-U-Net complex models relatively underperformed, indicated that architectural complexity does not enhance the segmentation performance of small subcortical structures. Descriptive Age-stratified analysis shows, ResU-Net maintained consistent performance across different age groups and 3D U-Net revealed strong age-invariance, however no statistically significant age-group differences were exhibited. Conclusions This study findings demonstrates architecture selection influences overlap, boundary detection and volume estimation small-structure segmentation and highlights the importance of evaluating model robustness to demographic variability. The findings offer a methodological benchmark for developing reliable SN volumetry tools for neurodegenerative research.

title: Long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation with intracanal bone fragment compaction for indirect anterior column support: a single-arm feasibility study in high load-sharing classification score thoracolumbar burst fractures.
abstract: Background Thoracolumbar burst fractures with high Load Sharing Classification (LSC) scores are mechanically unstable and associated with severe vertebral comminution and failure risk after short-segment fixation. This study evaluated outcomes of long-segment posterior fixation combined with intracanal bone fragment compaction as an indirect means of supporting the anterior column. Methods This retrospective study analyzed prospectively collected data from 121 consecutive patients with unstable thoracolumbar burst fractures (T10-L2) and LSC scores >6. All patients underwent open long-segment posterior instrumentation, decompression, and compaction of retropulsed intracanal bone fragments. Radiological outcomes included Cobb angle, percentage of anterior height compression (PAHC), vertebral body compression ratio (VBCR), and spinal canal compromise. Neurological recovery was assessed using the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) scale, and functional outcomes using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Results The cohort included 70 men and 51 women, with a mean age of 37.2 years and follow-up of 23.2 months. At final follow-up, 58.7% (95% CI 49.8-67.1%) achieved ASIA grade E. Significant improvements were observed in VBCR, PAHC, Cobb angle (15.6° to 7.9°; p = 0.008), and spinal canal compromise (65.2% to 8.7%; p < 0.001). Mean ODI improved from 59.4 to 8.4 ( p < 0.001). Conclusion Long-segment posterior fixation with intracanal bone fragment compaction was associated with favorable short- to mid-term neurological, functional, and radiological outcomes. Prospective comparative studies with CT-based fusion assessment, standardized safety reporting, and longer follow-up are required to confirm effectiveness and durability.

title: Supermicrosurgical perforator-to-perforator flap reconstruction for lower limb defects: a single-center case series.
abstract: Lower limb soft tissue defects remain a major reconstructive challenge due to frequent exposure of critical structures and compromised vascularity. In complex cases where local tissue is insufficient, free tissue transfer is required. Advances in supermicrosurgery have enabled perforator-to-perforator (P-to-P) anastomoses allowing reliable perfusion while preserving major axial vessels and minimizing donor-site morbidity. A retrospective review was conducted of five patients who underwent P-to-P free flap reconstruction for lower limb defects between January 2018 and January 2023. Preoperative CT angiography and intraoperative duplex ultrasound were used for perforator mapping. Two anterolateral thigh, one medial sural artery perforator, and two gracilis muscle flaps were utilized. Anastomoses were hand-sewn using 10-0 to 12-0 nylon under high-magnification microscopy. Flap perfusion was monitored with Vioptix Tissue Oximeter. The mean age was 60.8 years and defect sizes ranged from 5 × 4 cm to 20 × 8 cm. All flaps survived without partial or total loss. One patient developed minor wound dehiscence that healed without intervention. Reconstruction was successful across varied etiologies including infection, chronic wounds, and postoperative defects, with low morbidity and no re-explorations. P-to-P supermicrosurgical reconstruction offers a reliable, vessel-preserving approach for complex lower limb defects. This technique maintains major vascular axes, minimizes donor-site morbidity, and achieves outcomes comparable to conventional microsurgical methods across diverse etiologies such as infection, chronic wounds, and postoperative defects. In our series, flap survival was universal with no re-explorations and minimal morbidity. Wider clinical adoption and continued experience may further define its role in contemporary lower extremity reconstruction.

title: A Practical Pipeline for Patient-Specific Musculoskeletal Modeling: A Comprehensive MRI-Based Framework.
abstract: Patient-specific musculoskeletal (MS) modeling can provide estimates of internal joint loading that canot be measured directly. However, limitations in automated segmentation due to data-scarce environments, morphing difficulty caused by anatomical variability, and functional non-alignment are major bottlenecks that hinder the practical application of modeling and reduce productivity in musculoskeletal research. To comprehensively address these practical issues, this study proposes and validates an integrated, automated modeling framework.. First, we automatically segmented the lower extremity bones of the 4 knee osteoarthritis patients using a multi-atlas-based segmentation algorithm. By addressing key methodological challenges, this study will bring patient-specific models closer to future clinical application, where they could help assess individual loading across different activities and inform treatment and rehabilitation strategies.

title: Parameter analysis for diffusion tensor imaging corresponding to microstructural alterations following spinal cord injury.
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is a quantitative MRI technique that enables non-invasive, in vivo evaluation of spinal cord injury (SCI). Based on the anisotropy of water molecule diffusion, DTI provides superior detection of microstructural alterations compared with conventional MRI. Diffusion is quantified by parameters including fractional anisotropy (FA), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), average diffusion coefficient (DCavg), axial diffusion (AD), radial diffusion (RD), and mean diffusion (MD), each showing distinct temporal sensitivity to SCI. Changes in these indices reflect underlying tissue disruption and are closely correlated with neurological function in both experimental and clinical studies. Despite extensive investigations, a systematic summary of their diagnostic and prognostic value has been lacking. This review highlights parameter sensitivity at different injury stages and the associated microstructural changes. AD and DCavg demonstrated high sensitivity in the acute phase, whereas FA was particularly sensitive in the chronic phase. ADC and MD showed mild sensitivity in acute and subacute stages but became more relevant chronically, while RD exhibited low sensitivity in acute phase but progressively increased over time. Collectively, DTI provides critical diagnostic information, and cross-linked analysis of multiple metrics across time points enables more accurate evaluation of SCI severity and prognosis.

title: Retrospective multi-reader evaluation of a Deep-Learning-based cancer detection model in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the clinical impact of a deep-learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool applied to contrast-enhanced mammography on radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reading efficiency. Methods In this retrospective single-centre study, 150 contrast-enhanced mammography examinations were interpreted by five radiologists. Each case was read and annotated twice in two sequential sessions: first without assistance and then with the computer-aided diagnostic tool, with a minimum 4-week washout period. Diagnostic performance was assessed at lesion and breast levels using free-response receiver operating characteristic analysis, area under the curve, and false-positive rate. Reading time for one radiologist was recorded as an exploratory measure. Results The computer-aided diagnostic tool was associated with improved lesion-level performance for most radiologists, with a mean increase in the area under the free-response curve of 0.030 ± 0.018. At 89% sensitivity, false-positive findings decreased by an average of 11.4% ± 24% across all radiologists. No improvement was observed at the breast level, possibly related to the tool's single-view analysis and dataset characteristics. An exploratory analysis showed a 31% reduction in reading time for one radiologist. Conclusion Integration of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool into contrast-enhanced mammography was associated with improved lesion-level diagnostic performance and reduced false-positive findings, without measurable improvement at the breast level. Advances in knowledge To our knowledge, this study provides one of the early clinical evaluations of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool for contrast-enhanced mammography, suggesting potential improvements in lesion-level diagnostic performance and workflow efficiency while highlighting current limitations at the breast level.

title: Delayed diagnosis of congenital pulmonary airway malformation in an infant: diagnostic challenges and surgical implications.
abstract: Although congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) is usually diagnosed during prenatal screening, delayed presentation may increase diagnostic uncertainty and operative complexity. We report, to our knowledge, the first case of CPAM diagnosed and surgically managed in Syria in a 4-month-old infant presenting with a 1-month history of dyspnea, fever, and poor feeding in the absence of routine prenatal screening. Initial chest radiography, although technically limited, demonstrated a rounded opacity in the right hemithorax, while non-contrast chest computed tomography (CT) revealed multicystic lesions with a hyperattenuating intralesional component, raising suspicion for secondary infection or pleuropulmonary blastoma (PPB). The patient underwent right upper and middle bilobectomy, and histopathological examination confirmed CPAM and excluded PPB. This case highlights the complementary roles of postnatal CT, surgery, and histopathology in confirming CPAM and excluding PPB, particularly when delayed presentation increases operative complexity.

title: Internal herniation through Petersen's defect following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass presenting as subacute bilateral lower extremity edema due to IVC compression - a case report.
abstract: A 38-year-old woman with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) 2 years prior presented to the bariatric clinic on multiple occasions with postprandial abdominal pain and bloating and bilateral lower extremity edema. Abdominal pain did not improve despite antiacid medication and dietary recommendations. Computed tomography scan of the abdomen revealed an internal hernia (IH) through Petersen's defect (a potential space between the Roux limb and transverse colon), with a mass effect on the inferior vena cava by herniated bowel. Diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed the diagnosis. Reduction of the hernia and defect closure resulted in full symptom resolution. This case highlights the importance of high clinical suspicion for IH in any patient with a history of RYGB and abdominal pain, even when symptoms are chronic and/or atypical. Early recognition is important for prompt treatment and prevention of bowel ischemia and necrosis.

title: Emphysematous gastritis with extensive portal venous gas and endoscopic mucosal necrosis: gastric preservation despite an alarming presentation.
abstract: Emphysematous gastritis (EG) is a rare, potentially life-threatening condition. Extensive gastric pneumatosis and portal venous gas may suggest irreversible ischemia, although radiological severity and mucosal injury do not necessarily indicate transmural necrosis. A 70-year-old man presented with acute epigastric pain and vomiting. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated extensive gastric and duodenal pneumatosis with portomesenteric venous gas but patent visceral arteries. Immediately after CT, he developed cardiac arrest, with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 14 min. Emergency laparoscopy showed a viable stomach without perforation or transmural necrosis, whereas intraoperative endoscopy demonstrated extensive necrotic-appearing gastric mucosa. Gastrectomy was therefore avoided. Follow-up CT 4 days later showed complete resolution of pneumatosis and portomesenteric venous gas. The patient subsequently died from post-anoxic neurological injury and multiorgan failure. Surgical exploration and gastric resection should remain distinct decisions in severe EG, integrating imaging, endoscopy, and direct assessment of gastric viability.

title: MRI-Based Machine Learning to Differentiate True Progression from Pseudoprogression in Glioblastoma: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Differentiating true progression (TP) from pseudoprogression (PsP) after chemoradiation for glioblastoma remains clinically difficult. We evaluated externally validated diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based machine learning models and appraised study quality and transparency. Methods PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library were searched through October 1, 2025 (PROSPERO registration CRD420251144894). Eligible adult glioblastoma studies used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up. The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data; internal and combined internal and external test analyses were secondary. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with bivariate random-effects models. Results Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous. Conclusions MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.

Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Conclusions

MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.
